truths.truth: Detection names exactly which of tea/gh/glab resolve on the child's PATH, reports none from an empty stub dir, and spawns no forge CLI while doing it.
truths.evidence: Observed live with a controlled PATH holding only executable gh+tea stubs: {"ok":true,"action":"ask",...,"installed":[{"provider":"forgejo","bin":"tea"},{"provider":"github","bin":"gh"}]} - exactly the two, and neither stub's stdout/stderr appears. Same seam with PATH set to an EMPTY stub dir: {"ok":false,"action":"refuse",...,"installed":[]}, exit 1. Resolution is onPath only - cadence-core/bin/forge.mjs:264 installedProviders(onPath), and cadence-core/bin/lib/on-path.mjs:19 states no Cadence env override is read, so the PATH-injected stub exercises the production resolver (EXP-01). The no-spawn half is pinned by cadence-core/bin/forge.test.mjs:348 'detect: NO forge CLI is spawned while the defaults are derived (AC1)', which asserts spawned(marker) === '' - run by name, passes.

truths.truth: Both entry points reach the forge step inside their existing single-Bash setup chain, and a repository whose forge keys are non-null is asked nothing.
truths.evidence: cadence-core/workflows/new-project.md:74 and cadence-core/workflows/adopt.md:45 each carry `node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/cadence-core/bin/forge.mjs" detect --dir .` as the last line of the setup fence that already runs config.mjs get - no new turn. Both files then branch on `action` alone with all three arms present: new-project.md:84/87/90 and adopt.md:70/73/76, the `configured` arm reading 'Say NOTHING and ask nothing'. self-verify.mjs check 2 (invocations) is green, so those invocations match the declared CONTRACTS row. The ask-nothing half observed live: a repo whose config holds forge_provider/forge_repo/forge_host, run with a PATH carrying NO forge binary at all, answers {"ok":true,"action":"configured",...,"installed":[]} - the persisted record is consulted before any binary, so a configured repository is never refused for a CLI it does not need.

truths.truth: Where origin resolves, the slug is offered as a default and no provider is guessed off a host neither github.com nor gitlab.com.
truths.evidence: Observed live on two fixture repos. origin ssh://git@ssh.jcrenshaw.dev:2222/crenshawdev/cadence.git -> "defaults":{"provider":null,"repo":"crenshawdev/cadence"}. origin https://gitlab.com/g/sub/r.git -> "defaults":{"provider":"gitlab","repo":"g/sub/r"} (subgroup path intact). No host default rides any arm - envelope "host" stays null, which is D-08. Pinned by cadence-core/bin/forge.test.mjs:267 and :280 (both run by name, pass) and by cadence-core/bin/forge-decision.test.mjs:277, which asserts a slug failing isForgeSlug yields no default rather than raw text.

truths.truth: With the forge keys set and origin removed, the land-time tracker report resolves the persisted provider and slug instead of reporting no remote, and on Forgejo NAMES its login from the persisted host.
truths.evidence: cadence-core/bin/issue-check.test.mjs:793 'AC4: with the forge keys set and NO origin, forgejo still reports, bound by --login' - the fixture asserts `git remote` is genuinely empty first, then asserts action=report and that the recorded argv carries `--login work` (a login name the persisted host does not spell) and no `--remote`. :817, :837 and :857 cover the no-login skip, the unconfigured skip naming the keys, and a github record with no origin. All four run by name, pass. Independently traced end to end: `config.mjs set git.forge_provider=github git.forge_repo=crenshawdev/tracer` -> the pair lands in .planning/config.json -> `forge.mjs detect` reads it back as `configured` -> `issue-check.mjs check` records `gh issue list --repo crenshawdev/tracer --state all --json number,state --limit 200`. classifyOrigin is no longer called from issue-check.mjs at all.

truths.truth: Zero providers refuses ok:false with a hint naming an install, detail is null on the forge decision/create arms, and no forge-CLI stdout or stderr reaches any envelope.
truths.evidence: Live refuse arm: {"ok":false,"action":"refuse","reason":"no forge CLI is installed: none of tea, gh, glab resolves on PATH...","installed":[],"detail":null,"hint":"install the CLI for the forge you use - tea for a Forgejo or Gitea instance, gh for GitHub, glab for GitLab - then re-run this setup step"}. Leak probe: a `gh` stub printing LEAKY-STDOUT-TOKEN and LEAKY-STDERR-TOKEN and exiting 7 produced {"ok":false,"reason":"gh could not create o/r: the create command failed","detail":null,"hint":"run gh yourself..."} - grep for LEAKY over the serialized envelope: 0 hits. The child's stderr is discarded at the spawn (forge.mjs:159-168, stdio ['ignore','pipe','ignore']). self-verify.mjs is ok:true with problems:[] across all 26 checks including refusal-hints and undocumented-merge-warnings. NOTE, not a gap: forge.mjs's `usage` (line 501) and `internal` (line 513) arms do carry a non-null detail and no hint - both are the seam-wide documented exemptions in cadence-core/bin/lib/refusal-hints.mjs:74-77, the detail is text this repository authored (or a redactUrl'd JS message), and issue-check.mjs:366 carries the identical usage arm.

truths.truth: Creation runs one recorded argv per provider, private on all three, with the two arms whose argv wires no remote wiring origin themselves, and no argv is ever recorded without a prior confirmation naming provider, owner, name and PRIVATE.
truths.evidence: All four arms observed live against argv-recording stubs. github: `gh repo create o/r --private` then `git -C <dir> remote add origin <url>`. gitlab: `glab repo create o/r --private --remoteName origin` and no git line. forgejo, owner IS the login user: `tea login list --output json`, `tea repos create --name r --login forge.example.com --private`, then `git ... remote add origin`. forgejo, owner is NOT the login user: the same with `--owner acme` added. The same call without --confirmed emits ok:false with a hint and the argv log stays EMPTY - nothing spawned. Prose half: cadence-core/bin/prose-agreement.test.mjs:2510 asserts the four-fact confirmation ('Create <owner>/<name> on <provider> now? It will be created PRIVATE.') sits at an earlier OFFSET than the single `forge.mjs" create` invocation and that the invocation carries --confirmed; :2514 is its falsifier and reddens when the invocation is moved above the question. Both pass. cadence-core/bin/forge-decision.test.mjs:408 pins --private on EVERY row so a fourth provider cannot be added without a visibility pin.

truths.evidence: Not settleable from the tree. SUMMARY.md:61 asserts a live run on git.jcrenshaw.dev returned {"ok":true,...,"visibility":"private","remote_wired":true,"detail":null}, the repo appeared in `tea repos search`, an unauthenticated GET answered 404 and origin was set - then says the reachability clause was never proven and SUMMARY.md:50 records why (git ls-remote could not run: Host key verification failed, no TTY). human_checks.name: A real repository is created end to end on Forgejo
human_checks.expected: One real repository created through the shipped path on a live Forgejo instance, private, with origin wired AND reachable - `git ls-remote origin` in the new directory succeeds against the URL that was wired, which is the clause no earlier run settled.
human_checks.why_human: Out of reach, not merely unexercised: it needs a live forge account and an authenticated `tea`, plus an interactive TTY to accept the instance's SSH host key - the exact thing that stopped the previous run (`Host key verification failed`, recorded at SUMMARY.md:50). The throwaway repositories from that run were deleted, so no artifact remains to inspect, and the creation/visibility/origin half rests on the orchestrator's observation with no transcript in .planning/phases/1/reports/. Everything a stub CAN prove about this path is already proven (item 6).
